exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery, caesarean section)
lack of pre-natal risk information/informed consent
outcome: sepsis due to an infected haematoma
cohort: Twenty women who suffered unexpected obstetric complications and were involved in obstetric medicolegal reports prepared by a colorectal surgeon over ten years.
finding: Twenty women suffered severe obstetric complications, both from vaginal and caesarean deliveries, and were not informed of these risks prior to childbirth, leading to psychological distress and highlighting a need for improved informed consent.
mod_finding: Sixteen women who had vaginal deliveries suffered severe perineal trauma (third/fourth-degree tears, rectovaginal fistulae, stomas, faecal incontinence), while four women who delivered by caesarean section experienced post-operative complications (caecal perforations, small bowel enterotomy, sepsis).
